# Third-party images

Downloaded 2026-10-16 from Wikimedia Commons as Wikimedia's own PNG renders of the SVG
files (`upload.wikimedia.org/.../thumb/...1920px-...png`). Licences checked on the file
pages on that date. Used in Figure 2.1 (`fig:bg:eye-anatomy`) via
`images/scripts/fig_bg_eye_anatomy.py`.

| File here | Commons file | Author | Licence | Changes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `commons_schematic_diagram_of_the_human_eye_en_1920.png` | [Schematic_diagram_of_the_human_eye_en.svg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Schematic_diagram_of_the_human_eye_en.svg) | Rhcastilhos and Jmarchn (2007) | CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported | transparent background made white; resampled |
| `commons_macula_1920.png` | [Macula.svg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Macula.svg) | photograph: Danny Hope (Flickr "My Right Eye", via File:Righ eye retina.jpg); diagram: Zyxwv99 (2014) | CC BY 2.0 Generic | resampled only |

Notes:
- (a) is a horizontal section of the right eye seen from above (file description: "the
  lower part of the right eye after a central and horizontal section"), not a sagittal one.
- (b) is a right eye: the optic disc lies to the right (nasal). Its zone diameters are
  the figure's own: fovea 1.5 mm, parafovea 2.5 mm, macula/perifovea 5.5 mm, foveola
  0.35 mm, fovea-to-disc centre 4.5 mm, disc 1.77 x 1.92 mm.
- CC BY-SA 3.0 requires that an adaptation of (a) is shared under the same licence;
  `fig_bg_eye_anatomy_a.png` is such an adaptation.
